layout-patterns.name: Split Panel
layout-patterns.description: 50/50 vertical split with content on the left and a visual on the right (or reversed). The visual area bleeds to the edge. Content area has internal padding. Works well with a strong image or product screenshot. Can shift to 60/40 for content-heavy or visual-heavy slides.

layout-patterns.name: Editorial Stack
layout-patterns.css_grid_template: grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto auto; grid-template-columns: 1fr; max-width: 860px; margin: 0 auto;
layout-patterns.best_for: narrative slides,story telling,process steps,data-driven insights,long-form explanations,methodology
layout-patterns.description: Vertical editorial flow inspired by magazine layouts. Top: small uppercase section label or step number. Below: large headline (2-3 lines max). Body: 60-80 word paragraph in a comfortable reading width. Bottom: a pull quote, key stat, or visual footnote. Left-aligned reading gravity. White space is intentional.

layout-patterns.name: Dashboard
layout-patterns.content_areas: slide-title, metric-card-1, metric-card-2, metric-card-3, chart-large(colspan 2), insight-panel
layout-patterns.best_for: data reports,KPI reviews,analytics summaries,financial overviews,status updates,metrics presentations
layout-patterns.description: Top bar with slide title and time period. Three equal metric cards with large number + label + trend indicator. Below: a large chart taking 2/3 width and a insights/legend panel taking 1/3. Designed for data density without clutter. Uses subtle borders and background variation to segment zones.

effects-library.name: Dot Grid
effects-library.css_code_snippet: .dot-grid { position: absolute; inset: 0; background-image: radial-gradient(circle, var(--dot-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.15)) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 28px 28px; pointer-events: none; }
effects-library.description: Radial-gradient dot matrix pattern. Lighter and more refined than a line grid. Works on both light (dark dots) and dark (light dots) backgrounds. The 28px grid spacing is optimal for legibility — the dots register visually but don't compete with content. Zero JS, minimal CPU.

effects-library.name: Fade Up
effects-library.css_code_snippet: .fade-up { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(30px); transition: opacity 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .fade-up.visible { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
effects-library.description: The most universally applicable entrance animation. Element starts at 30px below and zero opacity, transitions to natural position with ease-out spring curve. Trigger by adding .visible class via IntersectionObserver or slide-enter event. Stagger multiple elements by adding transition-delay increments (0.1s per item).

effects-library.name: Progress Bar
effects-library.css_code_snippet: .progress-track { background: var(--track-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.1)); border-radius: 99px; overflow: hidden; } .progress-fill { height: 6px; border-radius: 99px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--accent-1), var(--accent-2)); width: 0%; transition: width 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .progress-fill.animate { width: var(--target-width); }
effects-library.description: Animated horizontal progress bar for showing completion percentages, skill levels, or agenda progress. The fill element transitions from 0% to the --target-width value when .animate is added. Gradient fill uses accent colors. Track has a subtle transparent background. Add a counter label that updates in sync for dual reinforcement.

adaptations.layout: RTL persistent sidebar and reading column, split experiment; stacked on phones
